The upper half of the disk forms a straight angle of \(180^\circ\). Reading the angles from left to right along the upper semicircle:

\[
40^\circ + (\text{shaded sector angle}) + 50^\circ + 30^\circ = 180^\circ
\]

Thus,

\[
\text{shaded sector angle}=180^\circ-40^\circ-50^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ.
\]

Since the point is chosen uniformly from the disk, the probability is proportional to the sector’s area, hence to its central angle:

\[
\frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ}=\frac16.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{6}}
\]
